clue.text: Scope that helps determine where one is

definitions.text: that helps determine where one is

blocks.note: first meaning: freedom of action, room to manoeuvre

blocks.clueFragment: that helps determine where one is
blocks.note: second meaning: the north-south coordinate used to fix a position on the globe

explanation.surface: Something that gives you the range to work out your whereabouts, like a navigator's instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scope' tempts as a telescope or sight; it is the abstract sense of room to act. The second half describes the map coordinate.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means freedom or leeway, and it is also the angular distance north or south of the equator used in navigation.

clue.text: Wearing fewer clothes, for example?

blocks.note: fewer garments means less
clothes you are wearing are on

explanation.surface: Is undressing a little an instance of something?
explanation.walkthrough: Wearing fewer clothes means having less on.
explanation.definitionFit: A lesson can be a warning instance, as when someone is made an example of so others learn.

clue.text: It marks a turning point when king takes subject out

indicators.note: the subject is placed on the outside, wrapping round what the king supplies

blocks.note: R for rex, Latin for king
a topic is a subject

explanation.surface: A chess or political moment where a king removes a subject.
explanation.walkthrough: T(R)OPIC. The tropics mark the latitudes where the sun appears to turn back, from Greek for turning.
explanation.definitionFit: Each tropic is the line of latitude where the overhead sun turns at the solstice, so it marks a turning point literally.

clue.text: The elite overthrow the drug men

indicators.note: to overthrow is to turn upside down, so in a down entry the next word is read upwards

blocks.note: pot is slang for cannabis
men in the general sense of people

explanation.surface: The ruling class topples drug dealers.
explanation.definitionFit: Top people is an idiom for those of the highest rank or influence, the elite of society.

clue.text: Decline of French production

blocks.note: de is French for of
generation means producing, as of electricity

explanation.surface: France's output is falling.
explanation.definitionFit: Degeneration is a deterioration or falling off in quality, which is what a decline is.

clue.text: One in position to fish

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means the first is placed inside the second

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
a place is a position

explanation.surface: Someone gets into position to go fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish' at the end looks like a verb completing the angler's plan; it is a noun naming the catch.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaice is a flatfish commonly eaten in Britain, so it is an example of the general category named.

clue.text: Novice takes ship in rather slowly

blocks.note: L for learner
the Argo was Jason's ship in Greek myth

explanation.surface: A beginner boards a ship at a gentle pace.
explanation.definitionFit: Largo is the musical tempo marking for a slow, broad pace, an Italian direction to players.

clue.text: Child legitimate, it's understood

blocks.note: an imp is a mischievous child
licit means lawful

explanation.surface: A declaration that the child was born in wedlock, it being taken as read.
explanation.definitionFit: Something implicit is implied without being stated outright, which is to say it is tacitly understood.

clue.text: Relief afforded by two measures in the Orient

indicators.note: the measures are placed in, so they go inside the region's name

blocks.note: em and en, two printers' units of width
the Orient is the East

explanation.surface: Comfort in the Far East comes from a couple of measures.
explanation.walkthrough: EAS(EM EN)T. Ems and ens are printers' spacing units, a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Easement is an old word for ease or relief from discomfort, as well as a legal right of way.

clue.text: Prevent young servant having something deducted from pay

blocks.note: to prevent is to stop
a page is a boy employed as a servant

explanation.surface: A young servant's wages are docked to stop him.
explanation.walkthrough: A stoppage is the British term for a sum withheld from wages, such as tax or insurance.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoppages are deductions taken out of wages before they are paid, such as tax or pension contributions.

clue.text: Slip so badly in examination

indicators.note: something done badly comes out wrong, so the little word before it is jumbled

blocks.note: to slip is to trip
taken as written, then jumbled

explanation.surface: A student blunders in an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tripos is the honours degree examination at Cambridge University.
explanation.definitionFit: At Cambridge University the final honours examinations are called the Tripos, so it is a specific kind of exam.

clue.text: Comic note can spoil accompaniment

indicators.note: to spoil something is to ruin its arrangement, so the letters are messed up

blocks.note: the letters of these three words are the fodder

explanation.surface: A funny note in a score may ruin the backing music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accompaniment' suggests music, but it is the abstract sense of going together.
explanation.definitionFit: Concomitance is the state of existing or occurring together with something, so it means accompaniment in that sense.

clue.text: Ring active girl

blocks.note: a ring is round like the letter O
live means active, as in a live wire

explanation.surface: An instruction to phone a lively girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive is a female first name, so it stands for a girl in crossword fashion.

clue.text: Go on, smile! It makes a change

definitions.text: Go on, smile! It makes a change

indicators.note: making a change to the letters of the words before means rearranging them

blocks.note: the letters of these words are the fodder

explanation.surface: Encouragement to cheer up, since a smile is a welcome change.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: rearranging familiar letters into something new is exactly what a coined word does to the language.
explanation.definitionFit: A neologism is a newly coined word or phrase, a change in the vocabulary, and here it is literally made by changing letters.

clue.text: Just estimation of price rise

blocks.note: first meaning: a fair judgement of worth
second meaning: an increase in value

explanation.surface: A merely approximate guess at an inflation figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' looks like 'merely', but it means fair or accurate.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both fair recognition of something's worth and an increase in the market value of an asset.

clue.text: Unintelligent being gets no change at vending machine

indicators.note: a change to the word before it means its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: an automat is a coin-operated food dispenser, or a restaurant of them in the US
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A dim-witted person is short-changed by a vending machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' looks like coins; it is the signal to rearrange the little word.
explanation.definitionFit: An automaton is a robot or someone acting mechanically without thought, so it is a mindless being.

clue.text: Shows they can't be thrown by starboard lights

definitions.text: they can't be thrown by starboard lights
definitions.note: cryptic: lights shining from the left side of a ship

blocks.note: first meaning: depicts

blocks.clueFragment: they can't be thrown by starboard lights
blocks.note: second, cryptic meaning: beams from the left side of a vessel, which the right-hand side cannot cast

explanation.surface: Something can't be done by lights on the right side of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Port is the left side of a ship and starboard the right, so rays from the port side cannot come from starboard lights; read as PORT RAYS.
explanation.definitionFit: To portray is to depict or represent, so it means shows in the sense of picturing something.

clue.text: Stopped when socialist captured the state

indicators.note: having captured something means holding it inside

blocks.note: a red is a left-winger
the US state in New England

explanation.surface: Things halted when the left seized power.
explanation.walkthrough: RE(MAINE)D. 'Stopped' here means stayed put, not halted.
explanation.definitionFit: To have stopped somewhere, in the sense of stopping over at a place, is to have stayed or lingered.

clue.text: Rate too highly cricketer's calculation?

blocks.note: first meaning: to judge something greater than it is
second meaning, whimsical: an estimate of an over, a set of six balls in cricket

explanation.surface: Someone thinks too much of a cricketer's arithmetic.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six deliveries from one bowler; the question mark flags the punning split into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: To overestimate is to value something above its real worth, and the split reading gives an estimate about an over.

clue.text: Girl to book one Italian forward

blocks.note: a woman's name
the New Testament, a book of the Bible
the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A girl reserves a football player from Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forward' looks like a striker in football; it is the Italian word for onward.
explanation.definitionFit: Avanti is the Italian for forward or onward, also used as come in.

clue.text: Stick notice in this place

blocks.note: an ad is an advertisement, a notice
here means in this place

explanation.surface: An instruction to put a notice up at this spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to cling fast or remain attached to something, which is what it means to stick.

clue.text: Convey with ecstasy

blocks.note: first meaning: to carry from place to place
second meaning: an overwhelming emotion

explanation.surface: Carrying something along joyfully.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means carry or move goods; as a noun it means rapture, as in transports of joy.

clue.text: Disunity shown in the former Yugoslavia?

definitions.note: a place found there: the port city in Croatia

blocks.note: first meaning: a division or rupture
second meaning: a Dalmatian coastal city

explanation.surface: The breakup of Yugoslavia as an example of disunity.
explanation.walkthrough: Split is a city on Croatia's Adriatic coast, once part of Yugoslavia, a state which itself split apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A split is a division or rupture within a group, which is what disunity means; the city shares the spelling.

clue.text: Made a proposal, but didn't stay

blocks.note: first meaning: put a motion forward at a meeting
second meaning: went elsewhere, changed house

explanation.surface: A suitor proposed marriage and then left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proposal' suggests marriage, but this is the formal sense of proposing a motion at a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: In meetings one moves a motion, putting it forward; and someone who relocated did not stay where they were.

clue.text: Records of female novices

blocks.note: a woman's first name standing for a female
L is the learner plate; two of them make plural novices

explanation.surface: The registers kept of women entering a convent as novices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novices' evokes nuns, but it is the learner-driver L, pluralised.
explanation.definitionFit: Annals are historical records kept year by year, so they are a kind of chronicle or register.

clue.text: Mention, as an example, solicitation

blocks.note: first meaning: to cite a case
second meaning: a request

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense survives mainly in the phrase 'at the instance of', meaning at someone's request.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means cite as a case in point; as a noun it can mean urging or request, as in acting at someone's instance.

clue.text: Caused a technical passage to be composed

indicators.note: a passage is a stretch running through the words, so the letters run across them

blocks.note: letters running from the end of the first word into the third

explanation.surface: Someone got a piece of technical writing drafted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composed' looks like written, but it means calm. The letters are caused / a / technical.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedate describes a calm, unhurried manner, which is what composed means when said of a person's demeanour.

clue.text: Average period in the interval

blocks.note: the mean is an average
a period is a time

explanation.surface: A typical length of time for an interval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the interval' points to the phrase 'in the meantime'.
explanation.definitionFit: The meantime is the stretch between two events, the same as an interval or intervening period.
